{
  "categories": [
    {
      "name": "indexes",
      "member": true,
      "evidence": "Modifies BaseIndex in src/index/base.cpp and subclasses blockfilterindex and txindex to parallelize initial block digestion across worker threads.",
      "band": "P2",
      "score": 0.68,
      "reason_tag": "speedup",
      "rationale": "Parallelizing block digestion tackles the multi-hour initial sync times of optional indexes, which is a major performance bottleneck for index users. Reviewers confirmed dramatic speedups for block filter indexing (e.g. Sjors measured a reduction from 35m15s to 4m26s), directly addressing the category's priority on sync time and resource use."
    },
    {
      "name": "tests",
      "member": false,
      "evidence": "The unit and fuzz tests added in src/test/ and src/test/fuzz/ test the new ThreadPool utility and index behavior rather than the test framework machinery itself.",
      "band": "Unranked",
      "score": 0.0,
      "reason_tag": "test coverage",
      "rationale": "Tests of specific areas or utilities belong with those components rather than in test infrastructure."
    },
    {
      "name": "utils",
      "member": true,
      "evidence": "Introduces a reusable general-purpose ThreadPool in src/util/threadpool.h with unit and fuzz testing.",
      "band": "P3",
      "score": 0.4,
      "reason_tag": "new feature",
      "rationale": "Adding a generic ThreadPool utility provides reusable threading infrastructure across the node. Within utilities, it is worthwhile internal infrastructure with clean test coverage, though secondary to the index performance problem it was introduced to serve."
    },
    {
      "name": "validation",
      "member": false,
      "evidence": "The PR changes optional indexes under src/index/ and does not touch validation code, chainstate, or block storage.",
      "band": "Unranked",
      "score": 0.0,
      "reason_tag": "speedup",
      "rationale": "Optional secondary indexes belong to the indexes category; the 'UTXO Db and Indexes' label applies here strictly to the indexes portion."
    }
  ],

    "leverage": 1
  }
}
